Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

delay verb

linger; hold someone or something up

also linger, tarry, stay on, loiter, hold up, detain, keep waiting

classical

Cic. Fam. 15.17.2: quod adhūc Brundisiī morātus es (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 7.40: iter (Lewis & Short)

moror, morārī, morātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent; without an object, or with the accusative of what is held up

linger, stay; hold up, detain

Nē multīs morer, to be brief (Cic. Verr. 2.4.104); nōn moror, I have no objection (Terence). From mora, a delay.

Examples

  • quod adhūc Brundisiī morātus es

    that you have stayed on at Brundisium until nowCic. Fam. 15.17.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • nē multīs morer

    to be briefCic. Verr. 2.4.104 (Lewis & Short)

See also put off, immediate, wait.
